seoTitle: Free JavaScript Regex Cheat Sheet with Examples
metaDescription: Searchable quick reference for JavaScript regex syntax: classes, groups, lookarounds, flags, replacement tokens and examples. Free, in your browser.
intro: A searchable cheat sheet for JavaScript regular expressions. It covers character classes, quantifiers, groups, lookarounds, flags, replacement tokens and a few ready-made patterns.
why:
Even regular users forget the small details: the syntax for a named group, whether lookbehind exists, what the s flag does, how to refer to a group in a replacement. Searching the web turns up answers for other languages with subtly different rules.

This sheet is specific to JavaScript. Type "lookbehind", "unicode", "flag" or "replace" and the matching lines appear with a short explanation. At the bottom you find starter patterns for dates, IPv4 addresses, hex colours and duplicate words. They are starting points to adapt and test, not complete validators; try them in the Regex Tester before using them.
howTo: Open the cheat sheet to see all entries.
Type a keyword such as group, lookahead, unicode or flag to filter.
Read the syntax on the left and the explanation on the right.
Copy a pattern into the Regex Tester to try it on your own text.

faq.q: Does it cover other regex flavours?
faq.a: No, it describes JavaScript only. PCRE, Python, Java and .NET share most basics but differ in features such as inline flags, atomic groups, possessive quantifiers and variable-length lookbehind.

faq.q: What does the u flag change?
faq.a: It switches on Unicode mode, so the pattern works on code points rather than UTF-16 units. That makes emoji behave as single characters and enables \p{...} property escapes such as \p{L} for any letter.

faq.q: Are the example patterns safe to use?
faq.a: Treat them as starting points. A simple email or URL pattern accepts many invalid inputs and rejects some valid ones. For validation, test with real data and prefer a dedicated parser where one exists.

faq.q: Where can I try a pattern?
faq.a: Use the Regex Tester on this site. It shows matches, groups and replace results for any JavaScript pattern and flags.
